transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As we prepare for the pilot of our live morning announcement broadcast, I need to complete the required review round before I can sign off on the operating and privacy plan. Mr. Greene, could you please provide me with the exact list of trained host students? Ms. Novak, I'll need the exact approved platform settings from you. And Mr. Ellis, please share the exact privacy restrictions and required records for this pilot. Once I have those three items, I'll be able to record the factual bases and make my decision on the plan.

transcript.text: I completed the broadcast practicum with six students — J1, J2, J3, J4, J5, and J6. Only those six have completed the school's camera, microphone, and live-broadcast training, so they are the exact list of students I can authorize as hosts for the pilot.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Ms. Patel, here are the exact approved platform settings: The district's approved student-media platform supports an internal-school audience only, with a 30-day archive, and requires moderator approval before each broadcast. I should note that the public-stream setting and 90-day archive in the draft plan are not approved district configurations.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Ms. Patel, I need to share an important privacy restriction. I reviewed a current court-related privacy order naming student K7 that prohibits the school from recording or broadcasting K7's image or voice. K7 is enrolled in journalism and must be excluded from both the host roster and any recorded broadcast, with this exclusion documented in the activity file. As for the required records for this pilot: the activity file must include documentation of K7's exclusion under the court order, the trained host list, the approved platform settings, and these privacy restrictions. Given the approved platform settings Ms. Novak described, the pilot must use an internal-school audience only with a 30-day archive and moderator approval before each broadcast — not the public stream or 90-day archive in the draft plan.
